html:
Eduardo Galeano was a Uruguayan journalist and writer, author of Open Veins of Latin America (1971), a passionate history of how the continent's wealth was drained by foreign powers.

Born in Montevideo, he worked as a journalist from his teens. Open Veins told the story of Potosí silver, sugar, rubber, coffee and oil as five centuries of plunder. It was banned by the dictatorships of the region, which only spread its fame. He went into exile in Argentina and Spain after the coup of 1973.

He later wrote Memory of Fire, a history of the Americas in short scenes, and Football in Sun and Shadow. Late in life he said he could no longer read Open Veins, finding its style too heavy. He remains one of the most read writers of Uruguay.
sum: Eduardo Galeano was a Uruguayan journalist and writer, author of Open Veins of Latin America (1971), a passionate history of how the continent's wealth was drained by foreign powers.
